newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Ping'an Insurance recorded premium income of $1.26 bln in 1996. [CORRECTED 10:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China's Ping'an Insurance recorded premium income of $1.26 bln in 1996. [CORRECTED 10:40 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and first paragraph to show figures are for premium income rather than profit.)

China's Ping'an Insurance Co recorded premium income of 10.5 billion yuan ($1.26 billion) in 1996, boosted by a booming life insurance business, the company said on Monday (corrects attribution from Xinhua news agency).
Premiums from life insurance alone topped 7 billion yuan, company officials said.
Ping'an had become China's second largest underwriter in terms of premium income, capturing 14 percent of the domestic insurance market overall last year, they said.
The company surpassed Shanghai's Pacific Ocean Insurance Co last year in overall premiums. State-owned People's Insurance Company of China was the industry leader.
Ping'an planned to boost premium income to 20 billion yuan in 1997, with life insurance accounting for 13 billion yuan of that, company officials said.
Ping'an held a 50 percent share of the life insurance market in the capital Beijing last year, generating 1.0 billion yuan in premiums, company officials said.
Chinese underwriters were increasingly focusing on the urban insurance market, official reports have said.
China has forecast its insurance market will grow to 200-250 billion yuan by the year 2000, up from 61 billion yuan in 1995.
